# Allowed combinations of options
#
# Polars: the release py-2.1.0 at the commit 7f902bd3ffd27ff82d14278a09a295ff2f7aed92 of vendor/polars.
# Generated from the catalogue and Polars by the engine test
# `allowed::tests::artifacts::the_committed_tables_are_what_polars_gives`, with Polars on
# one thread, so that a reason that depends on which of two failures comes first is the
# same every time. Do not edit.
# To refresh after a change of the catalogue or of Polars:
#   DAGEIST_REFRESH_TABLES=1 cargo test --offline --locked -p dageist-engine allowed::tests::artifacts
# See docs/how-to.md, "Refresh The Tables Of Allowed Combinations".
#
# Each line is: entry | receiver | options | outcome.
#
# The options are the flags and the choices of an entry, and the dtype a call is given.
# An entry with one option has a line for each value of it; an entry with more has a
# line for each pair of options and each pair of their values, so options that interact
# are all covered. A call that needs a dtype, as a cast needs the one it gives, has a line
# for each dtype alone and with each value that is not the default of each other option.
# A dtype is written as the tables write it, and may hold a comma, as `Datetime(us, UTC)`
# does. A flag is `true`, `false`, or `unset` where Polars decides. A method is run in
# `select` on a column of each receiver dtype, with the options it needs to mean anything:
# `over` is given `partition_by` and `order_by`, and an option that is given in place of
# another parameter, as a fill's strategy is in place of its value, is run without it.
# A step is run on the sample table, with what it needs: a join on `u`, a pivot of `a` by
# `g`, a rename of `a`, a sort by `a`.
#
# An outcome is `allowed <dtype of the result> <one|many>` (`-` for a step), or
# `refused <stage>: <Polars' reason>`. A combination is allowed only when Polars resolved
# its schema, ran it on three rows that include a null, and ran it on a table with no rows.
# The stage is where Polars refused it: `schema`; `rows`, when the schema resolved and
# the rows were refused; or `empty`, when only the table with no rows was. `one` is a
# value for the three rows together, `many` any other number. A reason is Polars' message
# up to its first blank line, on one line.
#
# 4052 combinations: 2699 allowed; 332 refused when Polars resolved the schema, 1021 when it ran the rows, 0 when it ran the empty table.
#
